title: curation-layer-for-safe-config-undo-with-trigger-explanations
creator: Liam Thompson
description:
Problem: Recent config rolls (batching/caching thresholds, runtime kernel selects) have caused subtle regressions — increased tail latency and token cost spikes — that automated monitors detect but lack human-readable rationale. Current auto-revert rules are either too aggressive (false positives) or too slow (miss extended cost regressions).

Proposal: Build a lightweight curation layer that sits between detection signals and automated rollback actions. The layer will: 1) generate an explainable trigger signature (human-readable rationale + ranked signals), 2) run a fast simulation on recent traffic to estimate cost/latency delta and regression confidence, 3) enforce guardrails and staged undo (dry-run -> canary rollback -> full rollback) with state reconciliation hooks to restore KV-cache/streaming session consistency where applicable, and 4) surface a compact decision log and remediation playbook to the on-call and SRE console.

Goals:
- Reduce high-cost false rollbacks and shorten time-to-recover for true regressions.
- Provide explainability so PMs/engineers can quickly accept or override an automated rollback.
- Ensure rollbacks are idempotent and reconcile runtime state (KV caches, batching windows, in-flight streams).

Acceptance criteria:
- Curation layer produces a trigger signature for >=95% of detected config anomalies, including top 3 contributing signals.
- Fast-sim (sample-based) predicts cost delta within ±12% of post-rollback observed delta in 80% of trials.
- Canary rollback path completes end-to-end in <5 minutes for typical config flips and has an automatic abort on worsening metrics.
- Decision log entry includes links to PR, simulation snapshot, and estimated token-cost impact.

Non-goals: full automated root-cause for every trigger; replacing human triage for ambiguous multi-signal incidents.

Design notes:
- Trigger signature: structured string built from ranked signals (e.g., "cost_spike:tokens+43%, tail_p95_latency+210ms, batching_drop_rate+12%") and normalized hash for dedup.
- Simulation: replay sampled requests against reverted config in an isolated sandbox using the latest KV-cache snapshot and traffic corpus from the last 30 minutes. Use continuous-batching emulator with real-world latency distributions.
- Guardrails: min-confidence threshold, cost vs fidelity tradeoff, customer-boundary policy (do not auto-rollback on customer-isolated Dedicated instances without human approval).
- Reconciliation: for KV cache, perform a prefix-quarantine flush sequence to avoid cache poisoning; for streaming sessions, gracefully drain and re-establish sessions with token offset reconciliation.

Telemetry and dashboards: integrate with Console to show per-decision cost curve, simulation vs observed delta, and rollback outcome (auto/approved/manual). Add a trace id to link logs, PR, and decision entry.

Docs & artifacts: Confluence design doc (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Config+Curation+Layer), prototype PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5428), simulation harness (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sim-harness/tree/curation-spike), dashboard mock (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4_DashboardMock), alert runbook (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Rollback+Runbook).
comments: 2026-02-16 - Liam Thompson: Spike completed. Collected 72 config-change incidents from the past 6 months and classified trigger signals. Found 3 common false-positive patterns: transient traffic bursts, downstream storage GC, and template changes that alter tokenization. Mocked an explainable signature format.

2026-02-20 - Asha Patel: Design review with SRE and PM. Agreed on staged rollback flow and customer boundary rule (no automatic rollback for Dedicated without explicit permit flag). Action: prototype simulation path and add KV-cache reconciliation prototype.

2026-02-28 - Asha Patel: Prototype PR opened: runtime PR #5428 includes a sandboxed fast-sim runner and a draft decision-log schema. Initial sim accuracy is within ±20% on cost delta for small changes; need to tighten sampling and warm cache handling.

2026-03-03 - Priya Rao (SRE): Ran runbook tabletop. Noted the need for abort hysteresis to avoid thrashing when metric noise is high. Suggested a min-stable-window of 3 minutes and a backoff factor between canary attempts.

2026-03-05 - Liam Thompson: Updated decision logic to include confidence bands and added a canary rollback timeout of 5 minutes. Opening a follow-up ticket to address heavy-tail latency simulations (ENG-???) and to add e2e tests for stream session reconciliation.

2026-03-05 - Asha Patel: Next steps: complete production-safe sim improvements, add console UI for approve/override, and run on-call shadow for two weeks in behind-flag mode. Planned rollout: behind-flag for runtime-1.24 canaries, then gradual activation tied to a telemetry-based QA gate.
